$comment: Source clearance registry. The fetcher MUST refuse any source where clearance != 'green'. Seed the `sources` table from this file.

sources.name: kulturdaten.berlin
sources.note: Berlin's official cultural data hub (Technologiestiftung Berlin, Senate-funded). Base layer. Build this adapter first.

sources.name: Ticketmaster International Discovery API v2
sources.note: Big venues, concerts, comedy, sport. Filter city=Berlin. Includes ticket links for later affiliate revenue.

sources.name: visitBerlin event calendar
sources.note: Official tourism board; they want redistribution. Read their data/partner terms (5 min) before flipping to green.

sources.name: Venue-published machine-readable feeds
sources.note: Highest merge priority. If a venue ships ld+json Event, .ics, RSS or /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events, it is published FOR machines. Probe each candidate venue for: /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events, ld+json in page source, /events.ics. Expected hit rate 30-50%.

sources.name: Hand-curated + user submissions
sources.note: 5-10 insider events make the demo feed feel Berlin-real. Later: venue self-serve portal.

blocked.reason: robots.txt disallows /api/, blocks commercial crawlers and all named AI agents; ToS forbids scraping. Their GraphQL endpoint is explicitly closed.

robots.txt technically permits crawling, BUT they are a direct aggregator and their event database is protected by sui-generis database right (§ 87b UrhG). Extracting substantial parts is the actual risk.
Official API only reads calendars you own (Luma Plus required). Page-scraping their aggregated database raises the same § 87b issue.
blocked.allowed_use: link out; revisit via official partnership

blocked.reason: robots.txt: Disallow /api/ for all agents, Content-Signal ai-train=no, all AI crawlers blocked by name.
